items.title: When Planning Problems Become Hard for LLMs: Separating Structural Complexity from Semantic Interpretability
items.one_liner: LLM planning failures stem more from predicate semantics than structural difficulty, proving that classical symbolic heuristics already estimate structural complexity well.
items.summary: Researchers examined seven STRIPS planning domains to distinguish structural difficulty from semantic vocabulary interpretation in LLM planning tasks. The zero-training delete-relaxation heuristic h_add outperformed learned alternatives like ridge regression, object count, and ARC for predicting structural difficulty on held-out domains with a mean Spearman |rho| of 0.931. To isolate semantic effects, the authors progressively renamed predicates while keeping states, transitions, and optimal plans identical, showing that valid LLM planning success dropped from 67.5% to 40.0% between 0% and 100% renaming. The findings indicate that symbolic heuristics already estimate structural difficulty effectively, meaning future hybrid planning improvements should focus on modeling LLM behavior sensitive to predicate semantics rather than building new structural predictors.

items.title: Energy Consumption of Post-Quantum Cryptography on Constrained and General-Purpose Architectures
items.one_liner: NIST post-quantum algorithms ML-KEM and ML-DSA are efficient on IoT hardware, but SLH-DSA signing incurs prohibitive energy costs on 32-bit devices.
items.summary: Researchers benchmarked the computational performance and energy consumption of the three NIST-standardized post-quantum cryptography algorithms—FIPS 203 (ML-KEM), FIPS 204 (ML-DSA), and FIPS 205 (SLH-DSA)—across 32-bit and 64-bit IoT devices and laptop hardware using OpenSSL 3.5 and a USB power meter. Results show that ML-KEM and ML-DSA deliver energy and speed efficiency comparable to classical elliptic-curve cryptography on all architectures. However, SLH-DSA signing proved highly inefficient on constrained devices, with energy costs up to 243% higher on 32-bit hardware compared to 64-bit systems, making it impractical for resource-limited IoT deployments.

items.bottom_line: Security practitioners planning PQC migration must avoid SLH-DSA signing on resource-constrained 32-bit IoT hardware due to excessive energy consumption.

items.one_liner: TURTLE uses an automated multi-agent framework to evolve self-tuning benchmarks for long-horizon AI tool use.
items.summary: Researchers have introduced TURTLE (Tool Use Related Tasks with Long-Horizon Evolution), an Unsupervised Environment Design approach designed to scale and automate data generation for long-horizon AI tool use. Using a proposer, solver, and feedback generator LLM agent structure, TURTLE dynamically evolves tasks across applications such as Gmail, Venmo, and Slack to target specific difficulty levels without human supervision. Evaluations using Gemma 4 31B-it on benchmarks including AppWorld, τ-Bench, and AutomationBench showed a 165% increase in the proportion of hard tasks and successfully elicited a broader diversity of failure modes.
items.bottom_line: TURTLE solves data scaling bottlenecks for tool-using AI agents by autonomously generating adaptive, increasingly difficult evaluation tasks.

claims.text: To make data generation scalable, we propose, TURTLE (Tool Use Related Tasks with Long-Horizon Evolution), an Unsupervised Environment Design (UED) approach to evolve existing tasks using a proposer, a solver, and a feedback generator large language model agents.

items.title: feder-cr/git-ai — Git designed for AI agents.
items.summary: Anthropic built Scion, a faster version control system for coding agents, and described it in Redesigning source control: a server-centric system built for hundreds of agents that read, write and land code at the same time. Scion is internal to Anthropic and is not available to the public. So I built gitai: an open-source version of that design that anyone can run, and that the community can improve and maintain together. Vendor neutral: the server never calls a language model, and every AI feature works with any provider, or none. gitai is an independent implementation of the publicly described design.
